title: AI crawlers
content: AI crawlers are automated programs that AI companies use to fetch web pages for model training, for search indexes, or in response to a person's request.

meta.why: Each crawler has its own user agent name, which means a robots.txt rule that blocks a training crawler can leave a search crawler allowed.
meta.example: A publisher blocks GPTBot to keep pages out of training data and allows OAI-SearchBot so the same pages can appear in ChatGPT search results.
meta.check: Read your robots.txt file and your server logs for the user agents each AI company documents, then confirm the rules match what you intend to allow.
meta.limitation: OpenAI notes that robots.txt rules may not apply to a fetch a person starts. Treat robots.txt as a rule for crawlers, and expect an assistant to reach a page in other ways too.
